name: BQ27441 LiPo fuel gauge (Battery Babysitter)
description: Texas Instruments BQ27441-G1 single-cell Li-ion/LiPo Impedance Track fuel gauge: reports battery voltage (mV), state of charge (%), average current (mA, via a 10 mOhm sense resistor), power (mW), temperature (0.1 K) and remaining / full capacity (mAh) over I2C at 0x55. The gauge is powered from the battery (2.45-4.5 V); VPU only feeds the I2C pull-ups. Sold as: SparkFun Battery Babysitter - LiPo Battery Manager (PRT-13777, BQ27441-G1A gauge + BQ24075 charger; bottom header GND, VPU, SDA, SCL, GPOUT, CE, plus VOUT, JST battery, micro-USB and VIN charge inputs on other edges), I2C address 0x55.
eli5: Sits between your LiPo battery and your project and tells your board how full the battery is, how much current it is using and how many mAh are left.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, common with the battery's negative and the microcontroller

pins.name: VPU
pins.description: Pull-up voltage input for the on-board 4.7 kOhm SDA/SCL and 10 kOhm GPOUT pull-ups; connect to your board's logic supply (3.3 V). It does not power the gauge, which runs from the battery.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7 kOhm pull-up to VPU on the board)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 kOhm pull-up to VPU on the board)

pins.name: GPOUT
pins.description: Gauge interrupt output, open-drain, 10 kOhm pull-up to VPU: pulses on SOC changes (SOC_INT) or signals battery low (BAT_LOW). A rising edge also wakes the gauge from SHUTDOWN. Optional.

pins.name: CE
pins.description: Charge enable of the BQ24075 charger, active low (printed with an overbar). Internal ~285 kOhm pull-down, so charging is enabled when left open; drive high to stop charging. Not part of the fuel gauge.

supplierQuery: SparkFun Battery Babysitter BQ27441 LiPo fuel gauge
buildNotes: Plug a 1-cell LiPo into the JST battery connector. Without a battery the BQ27441 has no power and does not answer on I2C; after connecting one, allow about 250 ms (tPUCD) before talking to it.
VPU is only the pull-up supply: connect it to 3.3 V on an ESP32/Pico (datasheet VPU range 1.62-3.6 V). Never connect the battery or VOUT to a GPIO.

Standard commands are 16-bit words, LOW byte first: Voltage 0x04 (mV), AverageCurrent 0x10 (signed mA), StateOfCharge 0x1C (%), Temperature 0x02 (0.1 K, minus 273.15 for C), RemainingCapacity 0x0C and FullChargeCapacity 0x0E (mAh).
Leave at least 66 us between I2C packets and poll each value no more than twice a second, or the gauge's watchdog can reset it.
Current is measured through the board's 10 mOhm sense resistor: negative while the battery powers the load, positive while charging.

The capacity and SOC estimates assume the default Design Capacity (1340 mAh on the -G1A). For a different battery, update Design Capacity in data memory (TRM section 3.1) or expect SOC to be off until the gauge has learned the cell.
VOUT (+/-) on the same edge is the charger's power-path output (3-5.5 V); it can power your project through its VIN pin, not its 3V3 pin.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from bq27441 import BQ27441

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
gauge = BQ27441(i2c)  # address 0x55; the gauge runs from the battery, so plug one in
while True:
    print('V=%dmV SOC=%d%% I=%dmA T=%.2fC RM=%d/%dmAh' % (
        gauge.voltage(), gauge.soc(), gauge.current(), gauge.temperature(),
        gauge.remaining_capacity(), gauge.full_capacity()))
    time.sleep(1)  # read each value at most twice a second (datasheet 9.5.4.3)

test.title: Reports the voltage, charge, current, temperature and capacity set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (3 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
